 Age Limit and Relaxation

  • Maximum Age limit: 56 Years
  • Age relaxation is applicable as per rules.

Upper Age limit will be as specified against each post

Applicants belonging to reserved category (SC/ST/OBC) / physically challenged/Ex-servicemen could be eligible for relaxations according to the ‘Government of India’ norms.

 Government employees on payscale will be eligible for relaxation in age by 5 years including  other  age relaxations as applicable.

 The cut-off date for ascertaining the age and experience will be Last Date of submission of    application.

Candidates seeking age relaxation need to submit a copy of caste certificate when called for document verification.  

 SSLC/SSC/ISC mark sheet/ certificate and any other valid document will be considered as proof of date of birth.

The Economically Weaker Section’s Certificate should be strictly in the format prescribed by DoPT.  The format is available on the website www.persmin.nic.in

The application of the candidates not meeting the prescribed age criteria will be reject/cancelled without any prior intimation.

Candidates belonging to OBC category (Non creamy layer) should produce the certificate issued in prescribed format.

Application Fee

  • No application fee is charged by C-DAC for applying to this advertisement.

Important Dates

  • Notification Release Date: 01-02-2026
  • Starting Date for Apply Online: 01-02-2026
  • Last Date for Apply Online: 20-02-2026
  • Interview Dates: Will be communicated via email to shortlisted candidates

Selection Process

  • Candidate should meet the eligibility criteria as specified in the advertisement.  
  • The qualification and experience prescribed, are the minimum requirements and possession of the  same does not automatically make the candidates entitled to be called for written test and / or selection processes. 
  • There will be an initial screening based on the academic records and other parameters declared in  the on-line application and only screened-in candidates will be considered for further selection process. 
  • The management reserves the right to increase/alter the minimum eligibility criteria/cut off  limits, in  the event of the number of applicants are more, for any post(s), at its discretion. 
  • Candidates will be selected on the basis of their academic credentials, experience profile, written   test marks (if any), performance in the interview and such other selection processes/parameters, as adopted and deemed fit by management. e. Mere application and fulfilment of the mentioned qualifications etc., does not entitle a candidate  to be called for written/skill test/ interview.
  • C-DAC may restrict the number of candidates to be  called to participate in interview/selection process to a reasonable limit, on the basis of qualifications and experience higher than that of the minimum prescribed in the advertisement. The  candidates should, therefore, furnish all the qualifications and experience possessed in the relevant field, over and above the minimum qualifications prescribed.  
  • The selection process shall be carried out by the respective C-DAC Centre based on its requirements and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further process.
  • All information submitted in the application will be verified with the original documents at the time  of document verification or at any stage of the recruitment process. If any documents/information provided by the candidate is found to be false or incorrect or Non- conformity with the eligibility criteria, then his/her candidature is liable to be rejected/cancelled at  any stage of the recruitment and selection process without any prior intimation.
  • The candidature is also liable for rejection at any stage if C-DAC comes across any evidence/knowledge that the qualification, experience and any other particulars indicated in the application/other    forms/formats are not recognized/false misleading and/or amounts to suppression of information/particulars which should have been brought to the notice of C-DAC

How to Apply

  • Before filling the online application form, Candidates should read General Terms and Conditions carefully.
  • Candidate should read all the eligibility parameters and ensure that he/she is eligible for the post before starting to apply online.
  • Candidate should have a valid email id and mobile no. which should remain valid & active till the completion of selection process.
  • While applying online Candidates can click on the ‘Apply’ button provided against each position for which he/she wish to apply.
  • The candidate needs to log in with mobile no. and then fill in the OTP received on the said mobile no.
  • On filling the correct OTP, the applicant will be directed to fill in the application form. In case you have filled in an application in our previous advertisement, the applicant will receive a prefilled editable application.
  • Candidates shall check the prefilled application and submit it, after adding additional details by clicking on ‘Submit’ button.
  • Candidates should scan their photograph in .jpg format (not more than 400 KB) and keep it ready before starting to apply online for uploading.
  • Candidate should upload their resume in PDF format (Not more than 500 KB)
  • A unique application number will be generated by the system, please note this application number for future reference and use. Candidates can take a print of the application form and keep it with them for their own records.
  • No hard copy/printed applications should be sent to C-DAC. Incomplete and defectively filled online forms shall be rejected straightway and no subsequent correspondences will be entertained in this regard.
  • Candidates working in Government/PSUs/Govt. Autonomous bodies should also apply online in advance and print of the application form, duly filled and signed should be forwarded through proper channel to HRD Section, C-DAC, Bangalore.
  • Those who are not forwarding their application through proper channel are required to produce 'No objection certificate (NOC)' from their current employer at the time of interview, if called for, failing which they will not be permitted to attend the interview.
  • Any dispute with regard to selection/recruitment process will be subject to Courts/Tribunals having jurisdiction over Bangalore, Karnataka only.

  • Stringers will be paid for coverages, irrespective of the length of footage or its usage, but inclusive of transportation and delivery charges.

  • (ii) In case of outstation coverage, which are coverages undertaken beyond the geographical limit of the District HQ where the Stringer is empanelled, the Stringer’s fee would be Rs. 1,800 irrespective of the length of the footage or usage of the coverage, inclusive of transportation and delivery charges.

Application Fee

  • Demand Draft of Rs. 1,180/- (inclusive of GST) towards non-refundable processing fee in favour of the “DDO, DDK, Kolkata” payable at Kolkata.

Important Dates

Last Date of Receipt of Application 04 March 2026 till 6:00 pm

Selection Process

  • Proof of ownership of the equipment must be submitted at the time of the interview, if shortlisted.
  • A physical verification of the equipment and documents will be done on the day of the interview.
  • A test coverage assignment will be given to all applicants for their submission to RNU before their interview date.
  • Submission of the test coverage assignment on time is essential for being called for the interview.

General Information / Instructions

  • Empanelled Stringers are expected to do news coverages and short features on news, current affairs, sports, business and other subjects. Applicants preferably equipped with four-wheel vehicles, should have qualifications, experience, and expertise in cinematography/videography/ news-gathering / broadcast journalism. Details of other terms and conditions prescribed in Guidelines issued by Directorate General, Doordarshan, New Delhi vide their Memo No. 3/4/2003-P-III dated 02.07.2010 are available in the Annexure to this notification.
  • Stringers should have adequate facilities and equipment to undertake the coverage.
  • The coverages by a stringer should contain all elements of a news story. For each coverage, the stringer should provide raw footage, press material and a script. Stringers should not only cover assigned tasks but also alert the RNU on major news fall/breaking stories/stories of interest in their area. The Panel of Stringers shall be revised every two years.

Stringers will be removed from the panel on all or any of the following grounds:

  1. When the Stringer refuses to cover the assigned coverages on two or more occasions;
  2. If the coverages are poor in content or in technical quality (poor audio quality, noisy video, variation in luminance level, defocused pictures, etc.);
  3. Delay in providing timely coverage;
  4. When the Stringer is suspected of subcontracting the assigned work to others;
  5. If the Stringers are found to be operating a cartel system among themselves;
  6. If the information furnished by the Stringer in the application form for empanelment is found to be incorrect.
  7. Any act on the part of the stringer that creates embarrassment to Prasar Bharati.

How to Apply

  • Applications duly supported with a Demand Draft of Rs. 1,180/- (inclusive of GST) towards non-refundable processing fee in favour of the “DDO, DDK, Kolkata” payable at Kolkata should be submitted in a sealed cover with superscription - “Empanelment of Stringers of RNU Kolkata, DD News- 2026” on or before the last date of submission of application.
  • The address for submitting the Application is: The Head, Regional News Unit, Doordarshan Kendra, 18/3, Uday Shankar Sarani, Kolkata-700095.
  • Proof in Duplicate of Academic and Technical Qualifications, Experience and Equipment ownership must be submitted along with the Application, whose model is given in this notification itself.
  • Separate Annexures can also be given along with the application detailing the experience or qualifications of the applicant and the team, if required.
  • For any clarification, write to [email protected].

UPSC CSE 2026 – Preliminary Examination Pattern

The Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination is the first stage of the UPSC selection process. It is a screening test used to shortlist candidates for the Main Examination. Marks scored in Prelims are not counted in the final merit ranking.

Paper Subject Type Marks Duration
Paper I General Studies (GS) Objective (MCQs) 200 Marks 2 Hours
Paper II CSAT (Aptitude Test) Objective (MCQs) 200 Marks 2 Hours

Prelims Key Rules

  • Both papers are objective type (Multiple Choice Questions).
  • Paper II (CSAT) is qualifying in nature – minimum 33% marks required.
  • Marks of Paper I are considered for cutoff and shortlisting for Mains.
  • Negative marking applies: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
  • Leaving a question blank carries no penalty.

UPSC CSE 2026 – Main Examination Pattern

The Civil Services (Main) Examination is the second stage and consists of a written examination followed by an Interview/Personality Test. Marks obtained in the written papers and interview are counted for the final merit list.

  • Selected candidates, who are already in service must produce a proper relieving letter / discharge certificate in original from their present employer at the time of joining, failing which they shall not be allowed to join the Bank.
  • Selected candidates (Deputy Managers), at the time of joining the Bank, will have to execute a personal bond for ₹ 3 lakh to serve the Bank for a minimum period of 5 years from the date of joining the Bank.
  • Any legal proceedings in respect of any matter of claim / dispute arising out of this advertisement and / or an application in response thereto can be instituted only in Mumbai and courts / tribunals / forums at Mumbai only shall have sole and exclusive jurisdiction to try any clause / dispute.
  • The Bank reserves the right to cancel the recruitment process entirely at any stage.
  • Candidates are advised in their own interest that they should not furnish any particulars that are false, tampered with or fabricated and should not suppress any material information while submitting application. At the time of examination, interview or in a subsequent selection procedure, if a candidate is (or has been) found guilty of: (i) Using unfair means (ii) Impersonating or procuring impersonation by any person, OR (iii) Misbehaving in the examination/interview hall or disclosing, publishing, reproducing, transmitting, storing or facilitating transmission and storage of contents of the test(s) or any information therein in whole or part thereof in any form or by any means, verbal or written, electronically or mechanically for any purpose, OR (iv) Resorting to any irregular or improper means in connection with his/ her candidature, OR (v) Obtaining support for his/ her candidature by unfair means, OR (vi) Carrying mobile phones or similar electronic devices of communication in the examination/ interview hall. Such a candidate may, in addition to rendering himself/ herself liable to criminal prosecution, shall be liable; a) to be disqualified from the examination for which he/ she is a candidate: b) to be debarred either permanently or for a specified period from any examination conducted by the Bank. c) for termination of service, if he/ she has already joined the Bank.
  • CANDIDATES REPORTING LATE i.e., after the reporting time specified on the call letter for Examination will not be permitted to take the examination. The reporting time mentioned on the call letter is prior to the Start time of the test. Though the duration of the examination is 2 hours 30 minutes, candidates may be required to be at the venue for about 4 hours including the time required for completion of various formalities such as verification and collection of various requisite documents, giving of instructions, etc.
  • In the examination hall as well as at the time of interview, the call letter along with original and a photocopy of the candidate’s currently valid photo identity (bearing exactly the same name as it appears on the call letter) such as PAN Card/ Passport/ Permanent Driving License/ Voter’s Card/ Bank Passbook with photograph/ Photo identity proof issued by a Gazetted Officer on official letterhead along with photograph / Photo identity proof issued by a People’s Representative on official letterhead along with photograph / valid recent Identity Card issued by a recognized College/ University/ Aadhar card/ E-Aadhar Card with a photograph/ Employee ID/ Bar Council Identity Card with photograph should be submitted to the invigilator for verification. The candidate’s identity will be verified with respect to his/her details on the call letter, in the Attendance List and requisite documents submitted. If identity of the candidate is in doubt the candidate may not be allowed to appear for the Examination.
  • Ration Card and Learner’s Driving License are not valid id proof.
  • Note: Candidates must produce in original the photo identity proof and submit photocopy of the photo identity proof along with Examination call letter as well as the Interview Call Letter while attending the examination/ interview respectively, without which they will not be allowed to take up the examination/ interview. Candidates must note that the name as appearing on the call letter (provided during the process of registration) should exactly match the name as appearing on the photo identity proof. Female candidates who have changed first/last/middle name post marriage must take special note of this. If there is any mismatch between the name indicated in the Call Letter and Photo Identity Proof the candidate will not be allowed to appear for the examination. In case of candidates who have changed their name, will be allowed only if they produce original Gazette notification / their original marriage certificate / affidavit in original.
  • 1. The examination will be conducted at venues given in the respective call letters.
  • 2. No request for change of centre/venue/date/session for Examination shall be entertained.
  • 3. Export-Import Bank of India, however, reserves the right to cancel any of the Examination Centres and/ or add some other Centres, at its discretion, depending upon the number of candidates, administrative feasibility, etc.
  • 4. Export-Import Bank of India also reserves the right to allot the candidate to any Centre other than the one he/she has opted for.
  • 5. Candidate will appear for the examination at an Examination Centre at his/her own risks and expenses and Export-Import Bank of India will not be responsible for any injury, expense or losses etc. of any nature.
  • 6. Choice of centre once exercised by the candidate will be final. If sufficient number of candidates do not opt for a particular centre for examination, OR if the number of candidates is more than the capacity available for exam for a centre, Export-Import Bank of India reserves the right to allot any other centre to the candidate.
  • Decision of Export-Import Bank of India in all matters relating to recruitment will be final and binding on the candidate. No correspondence or personal enquiries shall be entertained by the Export-Import Bank of India in this behalf.
  • Export-Import Bank of India would be analysing the responses (answers) of individual candidates with those of other candidates to detect patterns of similarity of right and wrong answers. If in the analytical procedure adopted by Export-Import Bank of India in this regard, it is inferred/ concluded that the responses have been shared and scores obtained are not genuine/ valid, Export-Import Bank of India reserves the right to cancel the candidature of the concerned candidates and the result of such candidates (disqualified) will be withheld.
  • There will be no sectional cut off but the final list for interviews will be drawn based on the candidate’s performance in the written test.
  • Instances for providing incorrect information and/or process violation by a candidate detected at any stage of the selection process will lead to disqualification of the candidate from the selection process and he/she will not be allowed to appear in any recruitment process of Export-Import Bank of India in the future. If such instances go undetected during the current selection process but are detected subsequently, such disqualification will take place with retrospective affect.
  • A pre-recruitment training will be organised for the candidates from reserved categories. Details of the training and its mode of delivery (online / offline) will be intimated to the candidates who opt for it through the online application form. Details will be shared with such candidates after the last date of registration.
  • Candidates whose writing speed is adversely affected permanently for any reason can use their own scribe at their cost during the examination. In all such cases where a scribe is used, the following rules will apply:
  • • The candidate will have to arrange his/her own scribe at his/her own cost.
  • • The scribe arranged by the candidate should not be a candidate for the same examination. If violation of the above is detected at any stage of the process, candidature of both the candidate and the scribe will be cancelled. Candidates eligible for and who wish to use the services of a scribe in the examination should invariably carefully indicate the same in the online application form. Any subsequent request may not be favourably entertained.
  • • A person acting as a scribe for one candidate cannot be a scribe for another candidate.
  • • The scribe may be from any academic stream.
  • • Both the candidate as well as scribe will have to give a suitable undertaking confirming that the scribe fulfils all the stipulated eligibility criteria for a scribe mentioned above. Further in case it later transpires that he/she did not fulfil any laid down eligibility criteria or suppressed material facts the candidature of the applicant will stand cancelled, irrespective of the result of the examination.
  • • Those candidates who use a scribe shall be eligible for compensatory time of 20 minutes for every hour of the examination or as otherwise advised.
  • • Scribe should not answer on his/her own. Any such behaviour observed will result in cancellation of candidature.
  • • Only candidates registered for compensatory time will be allowed such concessions since compensatory time given to candidates shall be system based, it shall not be possible for the test conducting agency to allow such time if he / she is not registered for the same. Candidates not registered for compensatory time shall not be allowed such concessions.
  • • During the exam, at any stage, if it is found that scribe is independently answering the questions, the exam session will be terminated, and candidate’s candidature will be cancelled. The candidature of such candidates using the services of a scribe will also be cancelled if it is reported after the examination by the test administrator personnel that the scribe independently answered the questions.
  • A compensatory time of twenty minutes per hour or otherwise advised shall be permitted for the candidates with locomotor disability and cerebral palsy where dominant (writing) extremity is affected to the extent of slowing the performance of function (minimum of 40% impairment).
  • Visually Impaired candidates (who suffer from not less than 40% of disability) may opt to view the contents of the test in magnified font and all such candidates will be eligible for compensatory time of 20 minutes for every hour or otherwise advised of examination.
  • These guidelines are subject to change in terms of GoI guidelines/ clarifications, if any, from time to time.

How to Apply

  • Candidates need to apply online only from January 26, 2026, up to February 22, 2026. No other mode of application will be accepted.
  • Scan their: Photograph (4.5cm × 3.5cm), Signature (with black ink), Left thumb impression (on white paper with black or blue ink), A handwritten declaration (on a white paper with black ink) (text given below), The consolidated Mark Sheets of Graduation and Post-Graduation, Graduation and Post-Graduation Degree, Caste Certificate (if applicable) Ensuring that all these scanned documents adhere to the required specifications as given in this Advertisement.
  • Signature in CAPITAL LETTERS will NOT be accepted.
  • The left thumb impression should be properly scanned and not smudged. (If a candidate is not having left thumb, he/she may use his/ her right thumb for applying.)
  • The text for the handwritten declaration is as follows – “I, _______ (Name of the candidate), hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required.”
  • The above-mentioned handwritten declaration has to be in the candidate’s handwriting and in English only. If it is written and uploaded by anybody else or in any other language, the application will be considered as invalid.
  • Keep the necessary details/documents ready to make Online Payment of the requisite application fee/ intimation charges.
  • Have a valid personal email ID and mobile no., which should be kept active till the completion of this Recruitment Process. Bank may send intimation to download call letters for the Examination etc. through the mentioned e-mail ID and / or SMS. In case a candidate does not have a valid personal e-mail ID, he/she should create his/her new e-mail ID and mobile no. before applying on-line and must maintain that email account and mobile number.
  • Candidates to visit Online Application and click on the option "APPLY ONLINE" which will open a new screen.
  • To register, choose the tab "Click here for New Registration" and enter Name, Contact details and Email-id. A Provisional Registration Number and Password will be generated by the system and displayed on the screen. Candidate should note down the Provisional Registration Number and Password. An Email & SMS indicating the Provisional Registration number and Password will also be sent.
  • In case the candidate is unable to complete the application form in one go, he / she can save the data already entered by choosing "SAVE AND NEXT" tab. Prior to submission of the online application, candidates are advised to use the "SAVE AND NEXT" facility to verify the details in the online application form and modify the same if required. Visually Impaired candidates should fill the application form carefully and verify/ get the details verified to ensure that the same are correct prior to final submission.
  • Candidates are advised to carefully fill and verify the details filled in the online application themselves as no change will be possible/ entertained after clicking the COMPLETE REGISTRATION BUTTON.
  • The Name of the candidate or his /her father/ Husband etc. should be spelt correctly in the application as it appears in the Certificates/ Mark sheets/Identity proof. Any change/alteration found may disqualify the candidature.
  • Validate your details and save your application by clicking the 'Validate your details' and 'Save & Next' button.
  • Candidates can proceed to upload Photo & Signature as per the specifications given in the Guidelines for Scanning and Upload of Photograph and Signature detailed under point "C".
  • Candidates can proceed to fill other details of the Application Form.
  • Click on the Preview Tab to preview and verify the entire application form before COMPLETE REGISTRATION.
  • Modify details, if required, and click on 'COMPLETE REGISTRATION' ONLY after verifying and ensuring that the photograph, signature uploaded and other details filled by you are correct.
  • Click on 'Payment' Tab and proceed for payment.
  • Click on 'Submit' button.
  • The application form is integrated with the payment gateway and the payment process can be completed by following the instructions.
  • The payment can be made by using Debit Cards (RuPay/Visa/MasterCard/Maestro), Credit Cards, Internet Banking, IMPS, Cash Cards/ Mobile Wallets.
  • After submitting your payment information in the online application form, PLEASE WAIT FOR THE INTIMATION FROM THE SERVER. DO NOT PRESS BACK OR REFRESH BUTTON IN ORDER TO AVOID DOUBLE CHARGE.
  • On successful completion of the transaction, an e-Receipt will be generated.
  • Non-generation of 'E-Receipt' indicates PAYMENT FAILURE. On failure of payment, Candidates are advised to login again using their Provisional Registration Number and Password and repeat the process of payment.
  • Candidates are required to take a printout of the e-Receipt and online Application Form containing fee details. Please note that if the same cannot be generated, online transaction may not have been successful.
  • For Credit Card users: All charges are listed in Indian Rupee. If you use a non-Indian credit card, your bank will convert to your local currency based on prevailing exchange rates.
  • To ensure the security of your data, please close the browser window once your transaction is completed.
  • There is facility to print application form containing fee details after payment of fees.
  • While filling in the Online Application Form the candidate will be provided with separate links for uploading Photograph, signature, left thumb impression and handwritten declaration.
  • Click on the respective link “Upload Photograph / signature / Upload left thumb impression / handwritten declaration/ other relevant documents”.
  • Browse and select the location where the Scanned Photograph / signature / left thumb impression / handwritten declaration/ other relevant document’s file has been saved.
  • Select the file by clicking on it
  • Click the ‘Open/Upload’
  • If the file size and format are not as prescribed, an error message will be displayed.
  • Preview of the uploaded image will help to see the quality of the image. In case of unclear / smudged, the same may be re-uploaded to the expected clarity /quality.

Eligibility Criteria

Educational Qualifications

  • Scientific Officer-E (Cardiology) - DR/01: MBBS + MD (General Medicine) + DM (Cardiology) with 2 years experience OR MBBS + DNB (General Medicine) + DNB (Cardiology) with 2 years experience
  • Scientific Officer-E (Hospital Administrator) - DR/02: MBBS/BDS + PG Degree or PG Diploma in Hospital Administration/Hospital Management/Hospital and Healthcare Management (minimum 1 year duration) + 8 years experience (3 years as Hospital Administrator in minimum 100 bed capacity hospital)
  • Scientific Officer-D (Hospital Administrator) - DR/02: MBBS/BDS + PG Degree or PG Diploma in Hospital Administration/Hospital Management/Hospital and Healthcare Management (minimum 1 year duration) + 3 years experience (2 years as Hospital Administrator in minimum 100 bed capacity hospital)
  • Scientific Officer-D (ENT) - DR/03: MBBS with MS (ENT) / MD (ENT) / DNB (ENT) from a recognized University
  • Scientific Officer-D (Radiodiagnosis/Radiology) - DR/04: MBBS with MD (Radio-diagnosis) or DNB (Radio-diagnosis) from a recognized University OR MBBS + PG Diploma in Radio-diagnosis/Radiology + 3 years experience after PG Diploma
  • Scientific Officer-D (Ophthalmology) - DR/05: MBBS with MS (Ophthalmology) or DNB (Ophthalmology) from a recognized University
  • Scientific Officer-D (Pathology) - DR/06: MBBS with MD (Pathology) or DNB (Pathology) from a recognized University
  • Scientific Officer-D (Anaesthesiology) - DR/07: MBBS with MD (Anaesthesia) or DNB (Anaesthesia) from a recognized University
  • Scientific Officer-C (General Duty/Casualty Medical Officer) - DR/08: MBBS from a recognized University with one year institutional experience
  • Scientific Officer-D (Nuclear Medicine) - DR/09 & DR/12: MBBS with MD (Nuclear Medicine) or DNB (Nuclear Medicine) from a recognized University OR MBBS + PG Diploma in Nuclear Medicine + 3 years experience after PG Diploma
  • Technical Officer-D (Nuclear Medicine Technology) - DR/10 & DR/13: M.Sc. with minimum 60% marks + Diploma in Medical Radio-Isotope Techniques (DMRIT)/Diploma in Nuclear Medicine Technology (DNMT)/Diploma in Fusion Imaging Technology (DFIT) with minimum 50% marks OR M.Sc. in Nuclear Medicine Technology with 60% marks
  • Scientific Officer-E (Nuclear Medicine) - DR/11: MBBS with MD (Nuclear Medicine) or DNB (Nuclear Medicine) from a recognized University with 4 years of experience after acquiring the prescribed qualification

Desirable Experience

  • For Technical Officer-D (Nuclear Medicine Technology): 4 years experience. Experience in full-fledged Nuclear Medicine Centre having PET/CT Scanner and GAMMA camera/SPECT/CT System will be preferred

Salary/Stipend

  • Scientific Officer-E (Cardiology, Nuclear Medicine) - Level 12: ₹78,800 + NPA (Non-Practicing Allowance)
  • Scientific Officer-E (Hospital Administrator) - Level 12: ₹78,800 + NPA
  • Scientific Officer-D (All disciplines) - Level 11: ₹67,700 + NPA
  • Technical Officer-D (Nuclear Medicine Technology) - Level 11: ₹67,700
  • Scientific Officer-C (General Duty/Casualty Medical Officer) - Level 10: ₹56,100 + NPA

Additional Benefits

  • Promotion opportunities for technical/scientific higher grades under Merit Promotion Scheme of DAE
  • Healthcare facility for self and family members
  • Attractive performance related incentive
  • Attractive professional update allowance
  • Departmental accommodation as per Government of India orders
  • Selected candidates will be governed by National Pension System (NPS) or Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) as per Government Orders

Age Limit (as on 27/02/2026)

  • Minimum Age: 18 years for all posts
  • Maximum Age:
    • 35 years for Scientific Officer-C (DR/08)
    • 40 years for Scientific Officer-D (DR/02, DR/03, DR/04, DR/05, DR/06, DR/07, DR/09, DR/10, DR/12, DR/13)
    • 50 years for Scientific Officer-E (DR/01, DR/02, DR/11)

Age Relaxation

  • SC Candidates: Maximum 5 years for post code DR/08 (which is reserved for SC category)
  • Regular Central Government Servants: As per Government orders for those who have rendered not less than three years continuous service in same line or allied cadre
  • Widows, Divorced Women, Women Judicially Separated: As per Government orders for those who are not remarried
  • Physically Challenged UR Candidates: Up to 5 years for Post code DR/08
  • 1984 Riots Affected: 5 years for children/family members of those who died in the 1984 riots
  • Kashmir Division Domiciled: 5 years for persons ordinarily domiciled in Kashmir division from 01/01/1980 to 31/12/1989
  • Ex-Servicemen: As per Government orders
  • Meritorious Sportspersons: As per Government orders

  • Application fee should be paid on or before 27/02/2026

  • Application number generated after submission is required for online payment

  • In case of high response, BARC reserves the right to restrict the number of candidates to be called for interview by conducting screening test of eligible candidates

  • SC/ST candidates called from outstation will be paid to and fro travelling allowance as per rules

Candidates may attach their CVs with the application form. However, applications with CV alone and without the prescribed form and certificates will be rejected.

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must possess the following qualifications as per UGC Regulations on Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and Academic Staff in Universities and Colleges and Measures for the Maintenance of Standards in Higher Education 2018 and its subsequent amendments:

For Professor Posts:

  • Excellent academic record with a minimum of 55% marks or equivalent grade at Master's level
  • Published work of high quality, actively engaged in research with evidence of published work with a minimum of 10 publications as books and/or research/policy papers
  • Minimum of 10 years of teaching experience in university/college as Assistant Professor/Associate Professor and/or research experience at equivalent level at the University/National level institutions with evidence of having successfully guided doctoral candidates
  • Contribution to educational innovation, design of new curricula and courses, and technology-mediated teaching learning process

For Associate Professor Posts:

  • Good academic record with a Ph.D degree in the concerned/allied/relevant discipline
  • Master's degree with at least 55% marks or an equivalent grade in a point-scale wherever the grading system is followed
  • A minimum of eight years of experience of teaching and/or research in an academic/research position equivalent to that of Assistant Professor in a University, College or Accredited Research Institution/industry excluding the period of Ph.D research with evidence of published work and a minimum of 5 publications as books and/or research/policy papers
  • Contribution to educational innovation, design of new curricula and courses, and technology-mediated teaching learning process with evidence of having guided candidates for research at doctoral level

For Assistant Professor Posts:

  • Good academic record as defined by the concerned university with at least 55% marks or an equivalent grade in a point-scale wherever the grading system is followed at the Master's Degree level in a relevant subject from an Indian University, or an equivalent degree from an accredited foreign university
  • Candidates must have cleared the National Eligibility Test (NET) conducted by the UGC or the CSIR, or similar test accredited by the UGC, like SLET/SET or who are or have been awarded a Ph.D Degree in accordance with the University Grants Commission (Minimum Standards and Procedure for Award of M.Phil./Ph.D Degree) Regulations, 2009 or 2016 and their amendments from time to time as the case may be
  • NET/SLET/SET shall also not be required for such Masters Programmes in disciplines for which NET/SLET/SET is not conducted by the UGC, CSIR or similar test accredited by the UGC, like SLET/SET

UPSC CSE 2026 – Preliminary Examination Pattern

The Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination is the first stage of the UPSC selection process. It is a screening test used to shortlist candidates for the Main Examination. Marks scored in Prelims are not counted in the final merit ranking.

Paper Subject Type Marks Duration
Paper I General Studies (GS) Objective (MCQs) 200 Marks 2 Hours
Paper II CSAT (Aptitude Test) Objective (MCQs) 200 Marks 2 Hours

Prelims Key Rules

  • Both papers are objective type (Multiple Choice Questions).
  • Paper II (CSAT) is qualifying in nature – minimum 33% marks required.
  • Marks of Paper I are considered for cutoff and shortlisting for Mains.
  • Negative marking applies: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
  • Leaving a question blank carries no penalty.

UPSC CSE 2026 – Main Examination Pattern

The Civil Services (Main) Examination is the second stage and consists of a written examination followed by an Interview/Personality Test. Marks obtained in the written papers and interview are counted for the final merit list.

Paper Subject Marks Nature
Paper A Compulsory Indian Language 300 Qualifying
Paper B English 300 Qualifying
Paper I Essay 250 Merit
Paper II General Studies I 250 Merit
Paper III General Studies II 250 Merit
Paper IV General Studies III 250 Merit
Paper V General Studies IV (Ethics) 250 Merit
Paper VI Optional Subject – Paper 1 250 Merit
Paper VII Optional Subject – Paper 2 250 Merit

Main Exam Structure

  • Total Written Papers: 9
  • Qualifying Papers: 2 (Indian Language & English)
  • Merit Papers: 7
  • Total Marks (Written): 1750

Interview / Personality Test

Stage Marks
Personality Test / Interview 275

Final Merit Calculation

  • Written Exam Marks: 1750
  • Interview Marks: 275
  • Total Merit Marks: 2025

Important Notes

  • Prelims marks are used only for qualification, not for final ranking.
  • Mains + Interview marks decide final service allocation.
  • Negative marking applies in Prelims only.
  • Candidates must qualify in both language papers to have their merit papers evaluated.

  • Complete One-Time Registration (URN)
  • Fill Civil Services Examination 2026 form
  • Upload photo, signature, and documents
  • Pay application fee (if applicable)
  • Submit form before 24 February 2026

General Instructions for Indian Bank Officer/ Clerk Recruitment 2026

  • Candidates should satisfy themselves about their eligibility as on the date of eligibility.

However, eligible outstation SC/ST candidates, called for interview will be eligible for reimbursement of II class to & fro train / bus fare or actual expenses incurred, whichever is less, by shortest route on production of proof of travel (rail/ bus ticket etc.) and Caste Certificate.

  • Canvassing in any form will be a disqualification.
  • The Bank shall not entertain any requests in any form like Post, Email, Telephone calls, in person, by hand, etc. from the candidate seeking advice/clarification about their eligibility to apply.
  • Any resultant dispute arising out of this advertisement shall be subject to the sole jurisdiction of the Courts situated in Chennai only.
  • Sportspersons who are currently under suspension/barred from playing by any regulatory authorities are not eligible to apply.
  • Bank reserves the right to cancel the recruitment process partly/entirely at any time, if required, without issuing any further notice or assigning any reason thereof.

Selection Process for RRB Group D CEN 09/2025

The recruitment consists of 4 successive stages:

Stage 1: Computer Based Test (CBT)

Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for candidates using scribe)

Total Questions: 100 (Each of 1 mark)

Subject Number of Questions
General Science 25
Mathematics 25
General Intelligence and Reasoning 30
General Awareness and Current Affairs 20
TOTAL 100 Questions = 100 Marks

Exam Pattern:

  • Objective type with multiple choices
  • Questions available in English, Hindi, and 13 regional languages (Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu)
  • Negative Marking: 1/3 mark deducted for each wrong answer
  • Section-wise distribution may vary slightly in actual exam

Minimum Qualifying Marks:

  • UR: 40%
  • EWS: 40%
  • OBC-NCL: 30%
  • SC: 30%
  • ST: 30%
  • PwBD: May be relaxed by 2 marks in case of shortage

Syllabus (Indicative):

  • Mathematics: Number system, BODMAS, Decimals, Fractions, LCM, HCF, Ratio & Proportion, Percentages, Mensuration, Time & Work, Time & Distance, Simple & Compound Interest, Profit & Loss, Algebra, Geometry, Trigonometry, Elementary Statistics, Square root, Age Calculations, Calendar & Clock, Pipes & Cistern
  • General Intelligence & Reasoning: Analogies, Alphabetical & Number Series, Coding & Decoding, Mathematical operations, Relationships, Syllogism, Jumbling, Venn Diagram, Data Interpretation & Sufficiency, Conclusions & Decision making, Similarities & Differences, Analytical Reasoning, Classification, Directions, Statement-Arguments & Assumptions
  • General Science: Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences of 10th standard level (CBSE)
  • General Awareness & Current Affairs: Science & Technology, Sports, Culture, Personalities, Economics, Politics, and other important subjects

Normalization: Marks will be normalized if CBT conducted in multiple sessions

Stage 2: Physical Efficiency Test (PET)

Shortlisting: 3 times the total vacancies (may vary) based on CBT merit

Nature: Qualifying (Mandatory to pass - marks not counted for final merit)

Candidate Type Test 1: Weight Carrying Test 2: Running
Male Candidates Lift and carry 35 kg weight for 100 meters in 2 minutes (in one chance, without putting down) Run 1000 meters in 4 minutes 15 seconds (in one chance)
Female Candidates Lift and carry 20 kg weight for 100 meters in 2 minutes (in one chance, without putting down) Run 1000 meters in 5 minutes 40 seconds (in one chance)
Transgender Candidates Same relaxed standards as Female candidates

Important PET Notes:

  • Two-stage test: First weight carrying, then running (after recovery gap)
  • Failing in weight carrying means elimination (no running test)
  • Weight carrying involves lifting sandbag (without handle) from waist-height bench and carrying without dropping
  • Candidates' responsibility to ensure medical fitness for PET - Railways not responsible for injuries
  • Exemptions from PET:
    • Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) - must pass medical examination
    • Course Completed Act Apprentices (CCAA)
    • Ex-Servicemen (ExSM)
  • Pregnant Candidates: Must submit self-declaration. If pregnant, PET deferred till 6 weeks post-confinement. Vacancy kept reserved.

Stage 3: Document Verification (DV)

  • Shortlisting: 1:1 ratio of vacancies based on CBT merit + PET qualification
  • Candidates must produce original certificates
  • No additional time given - absence leads to candidature cancellation
  • Scanned copies to be uploaded before DV at https://oirms-ir.gov.in/rrbdv
  • Certificates must be in English/Hindi (translated version required otherwise)
  • Hard copy of signed application form to be brought

Stage 4: Medical Examination (ME)

  • Conducted by Railway Medical Authorities
  • Must pass requisite medical fitness test as per IRMM
  • Visual acuity standards strictly enforced
  • Medical appeal option available (one final opportunity on payment)
  • Candidates found medically unsuitable will NOT be given alternative appointment

Final Merit & Selection

  • Based on CBT marks (after normalization if applicable)
  • Subject to PET qualification, DV clearance, and medical fitness
  • Post/Railway allotment as per candidate's preference, merit, medical fitness, and vacancy
  • In case of tie: Older candidate ranked higher; if age also same, alphabetical order of name (A to Z)
  • No right to appointment - RRB/RRC only recommends; appointment by Railway Administration

Reservation & Relaxation for RRB Group D CEN 09/2025

Vertical Reservation (Community-wise):

  • SC (Scheduled Caste)
  • ST (Scheduled Tribe)
  • OBC-NCL (Other Backward Classes - Non Creamy Layer)
  • EWS (Economically Weaker Sections)

Horizontal Reservation (across all communities):

  • Ex-Servicemen (ExSM)
  • Course Completed Act Apprentices (CCAA) trained in Railway Establishments
  • Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)

Important Reservation Rules:

For OBC-NCL Candidates:

  • Must produce OBC-NCL certificate issued on or after 01.04.2025 but not later than 02.03.2026
  • Certificate must be as per central list (http://www.ncbc.nic.in)
  • Must submit self-declaration (Annexure IIA) at DV that they don't belong to Creamy Layer
  • Certificate must mention: "Does NOT belong to Creamy Layer as per DOPT OM 36012/22/93-Estt.(SCT) dated 08.09.93, modified vide OM 36033/1/2013-Estt.(Res.) dated 13.09.2017"
  • OBC in state list but not in central list: NOT eligible for reservation

For EWS Candidates:

  • NOT covered under SC/ST/OBC-NCL
  • Gross annual family income < Rs. 8 lakh for F.Y. 2024-25
  • Family should NOT own:
    • 5 acres or more of agricultural land, OR
    • Residential flat of 1000 sq. ft. or more, OR
    • Residential plot of 100 sq. yards or more (notified municipalities), OR
    • Residential plot of 200 sq. yards or more (other areas)
  • Family: Applicant, parents, siblings <18 years, spouse, children <18 years
  • Must possess valid Income & Asset Certificate (Annexure III) based on F.Y. 2024-25 income/assets

For PwBD Candidates:

  • Minimum 40% benchmark disability required for reservation/relaxation
  • Certificate as per Form V/VI of RPwD Rules 2024 (Annexure V-A/V-B)
  • Must submit Unique Disability Identity (UDID)
  • Suitability for posts indicated in Annexure-A
  • Eligible Disabilities:
    • VI (Visually Impaired): Blindness (B), Low Vision (LV)
    • HI (Hearing Impaired): Deaf (D), Hard of Hearing (HH)
    • LD (Locomotor Disability): OA, OL, OAL, BL, LC, DW, AAV, CP, SD (without neurological/limb dysfunction), SI (without neurological/limb dysfunction)
    • MD (Multiple Disabilities)
  • Temporary disability candidates NOT eligible for reservation (as per DePwD OM dated 17.12.2025)

For Ex-Servicemen (ExSM):

  • Must have valid Ex-Serviceman Certificate from Zila Sainik Board
  • Serving defense personnel expected to be released within 1 year can also apply
  • Must submit NOC with probable discharge date (Annexure VI-A) at DV
  • Declaration/Undertaking (Annexure VI) required at DV
  • ExSM who already secured civil employment using ExSM quota: NOT eligible for ExSM reservation (only age relaxation available)
  • Different medical standards applicable (Para 534 of IRMM)

For CCAA (Railway Establishments):

  • Must have completed Act Apprenticeship by 02.03.2026 (appeared in NCVT exam)
  • National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) from NCVT required at DV
  • Weightage: 1/3rd marks from NCVT examination added to CBT marks for merit
  • If NCVT weightage gives lower score, higher of the two will be considered
  • Exempted from PET
  • Can apply to any RRB (not just training Railway)

General Instructions for RRB Group D CEN 09/2025

Application Rules:

  • ONE application per candidate - Multiple applications will lead to rejection of ALL applications and debarment from future RRB/RRC exams
  • Choose only ONE RRB/Railway Zone (cannot be changed later)
  • Indicate post preferences within chosen Railway Zone
  • Partial options allowed (will be considered only for opted posts)
  • No change in preferences after submission
  • Online application only through official RRB websites (listed in Para 24.0)

Identity Authentication:

  • Strongly advised to authenticate using DigiLocker or Aadhaar during account creation
  • Aadhaar-seeded bank account mandatory for fee refund
  • Candidates using alternate Photo IDs will face stricter scrutiny at all stages

Account Creation:

  • If already created account for CEN 2024/2025, use same credentials
  • Valid mobile number and email ID mandatory (will remain unchanged throughout recruitment)
  • Details in 'Create an Account' form CANNOT be modified

Application Modification:

  • Allowed from 05.03.2026 to 14.03.2026
  • Fee: Rs. 250/- per modification (non-refundable)
  • Can modify any number of times (except 'Create Account' details and Chosen Railway)
  • If changing from SC/ST to UR/OBC/EWS or from ExSM/Female/PwBD to non-reserved: Pay fee difference (Rs. 250/-) in addition to modification fee
  • No modifications entertained after 14.03.2026

Live Photo & Signature Upload:

  • Live Photo: Captured during application (NOT pre-existing photo)
  • Stand/sit in front of camera at eye level, face centered, neutral expression
  • Non-white clothing (preferably dark colors), no cap/mask/glasses
  • Applications with blurred/non-compliant photos liable for rejection
  • Signature: Running handwriting in black ink on white paper (scanned)
  • NO BLOCK/CAPITAL/DISJOINTED LETTERS
  • JPG/JPEG format, 30-49 KB, 140×60 pixels minimum
  • Signature must match at all stages (CBT/DV/ME/Appointment)

Scribe Facility (for eligible PwBD candidates):

  • Eligible: Blindness, Locomotor Disability (Both Arms - BA), Cerebral Palsy
  • Others: Only with certificate from CMO/Civil Surgeon (Annexure V-G)
  • PwBD <40% with writing difficulty: Certificate as per Annexure V-E required
  • Scribe must register at rrbapply.gov.in (One-Time Registration - OTR)
  • Candidate must enter scribe's OTR number during 15.03.2026 to 19.03.2026 window
  • Scribe qualification: ONE step below candidate's qualification
  • One scribe per candidate; scribe cannot be a candidate in same CEN
  • Compensatory time: 20 minutes per hour of examination

Examination Centers:

  • Allocated based on technical/logistical feasibility
  • Candidates may have to travel to other cities/states
  • No change of center/date/shift allowed

Banned Items at Exam Center:

  • Mobile phones, pagers, watches, earphones, Bluetooth devices, microphones, health bands
  • Calculators, books, pen, paper, pencil, eraser, pouch, scale, writing pad
  • Belts, handbags, caps, purses, cameras, water bottles, food items
  • ONLY e-call letter allowed inside test center
  • Pen will be provided during exam
  • No cloak room - advised not to bring valuables
  • Do not apply henna on hands/feet (obstructs biometric capture)

Important Warnings:

  • Debarment for life if found using unfair means, impersonation, forgery, misbehavior
  • Provisions of "The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024" applicable
  • Comprehensive post-exam analysis (log analysis, photo/biometric verification, CCTV review)
  • Beware of touts and fake websites - RRBs NEVER appoint agents/coaching centers
  • Selection purely on merit

How to Apply for RRB Group D CEN 09/2025

Step 1: Create an Account (if not already created)

  • Visit official RRB website from the list at Para 24.0
  • Click on "Create an Account" link
  • Authenticate using DigiLocker/Aadhaar (strongly recommended)
  • Enter valid mobile number and email ID (CANNOT be changed later)
  • Complete OTP verification
  • Create login credentials

Step 2: Fill Online Application

  • Login with created credentials
  • Select CEN 09/2025
  • Choose ONE RRB/Railway Zone (CANNOT be changed)
  • Fill personal details, educational qualifications
  • Select post preferences within chosen Railway
  • Choose examination language (English/Hindi/Regional)
  • Capture live photograph using webcam/mobile camera
  • Upload scanned signature (JPG/JPEG, 30-49 KB, black ink, running handwriting)
  • Upload SC/ST certificate (if claiming free travel pass)
  • Indicate scribe requirement (if applicable)
  • Verify all details carefully

Step 3: Pay Application Fee

  • Select payment mode: Internet Banking/Debit Card/Credit Card/UPI
  • Pay Rs. 500/- (General/EWS/OBC-NCL Male) or Rs. 250/- (SC/ST/PwBD/Female/ExSM/Transgender/Minorities/EBC)
  • Complete payment (all service charges borne by candidate)
  • Save payment receipt

Step 4: Final Submission

  • After successful payment, application will be accepted
  • Receive confirmation via SMS and email
  • Download and save final application form
  • Note Application Number for future reference

Step 5: Modification (if required)

  • Window: 05.03.2026 to 14.03.2026
  • Login and modify details (except Create Account info & Chosen Railway)
  • Pay Rs. 250/- per modification
  • Pay additional fee if changing from reserved to unreserved category

Step 6: Enter Scribe Details (if applicable)

  • Window: 15.03.2026 to 19.03.2026
  • Login to application portal
  • Enter scribe's OTR number
  • Enter OTP sent to scribe's mobile to confirm

Documents to Upload:

  1. Live photograph (captured during application)
  2. Signature (scanned - JPG/JPEG, 30-49 KB, running handwriting)
  3. SC/ST certificate (PDF, <400 KB) - if claiming free travel pass

Documents Required at DV (Original + 2 self-attested photocopies):

  • 10th/Matriculation certificate (for age & education)
  • ITI/NAC certificate (if applicable)
  • SC/ST certificate (Annexure-I)
  • OBC-NCL certificate (Annexure-II) - issued on/after 01.04.2025
  • OBC-NCL self-declaration (Annexure-II A)
  • EWS certificate (Annexure-III) - valid for 2025-26, based on F.Y. 2024-25
  • EBC certificate (Annexure-III A) / BPL card / Izzat MST (if claimed fee concession)
  • Minority affidavit on non-judicial stamp paper (Annexure-IV)
  • PwBD certificate (Annexure V-A/V-B) with UDID
  • ExSM certificate from Zila Sainik Board
  • ExSM declaration (Annexure VI)
  • ExSM NOC with probable discharge date (Annexure VI-A) - if serving
  • CCAA - NAC certificate from NCVT
  • LASIK declaration (Annexure-VII) - for A2/A3 posts
  • NOC from employer (if Govt. employee)
  • Caste change certificates (if name differs from 10th certificate)
  • Medical certificates (for scribe eligibility - Annexure V-E/V-F/V-G)

Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test for Working Teachers 2026 is a special TET conducted by the Tamil Nadu Teachers Recruitment Board (TRB) to help in-service teachers qualify the mandatory eligibility test for teaching Classes 1 to 8.

The Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test (TNTET) is a state-level examination that assesses the eligibility of candidates to teach in primary and upper primary schools. The 2026 edition is special as it focuses exclusively on working teachers, providing them an opportunity to clear the test amid government directives making TET mandatory for promotions and continued service. This is particularly relevant following recent G.O.s and court rulings emphasizing TET qualification for in-service educators. Working teachers in government, aided, and recognized private schools should read this article to understand application details, preparation strategies, and benefits.

Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test for Working Teachers 2026 – Complete Guide

The Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test for Working Teachers 2026 is designed to certify the eligibility of in-service teachers for teaching positions in Classes 1 to 8. Conducted by the Teachers Recruitment Board (TRB) under the Government of Tamil Nadu, it targets working teachers appointed before a specified cutoff date. The exam is held in offline mode using OMR sheets, with two separate papers: Paper 1 for Classes 1–5 and Paper 2 for Classes 6–8.

What is Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test for Working Teachers 2026?

TET is a state-level eligibility test for teachers of Classes 1–8 in government and aided schools, ensuring they meet national standards for teaching aptitude and subject knowledge. The 2026 version includes a special focus on working teachers who have not yet cleared TET, aligning with government and Supreme Court directives to make it mandatory for all educators. Clearing TET is now essential for job security and career advancement in Tamil Nadu.

  • Conducting body: Teachers Recruitment Board (TRB), Government of Tamil Nadu
  • Level: State-level eligibility test
  • Applicable classes: Paper 1 – Classes 1–5, Paper 2 – Classes 6–8

Special TET 2026 for Working Teachers – Key Highlights

This special TET targets working teachers, offering a dedicated chance to qualify without competing with fresh candidates. It differs by restricting eligibility to in-service educators, emphasizing their need for TET clearance for promotions and regularization. The test follows the standard TNTET pattern and syllabus.

Aspect Details
Exam name Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test (Special TET) 2026 for Working Teachers
Conducting body Teachers Recruitment Board (TRB), Tamil Nadu
Eligible group In-service teachers of Classes 1–8 who have not yet cleared TET
Papers Paper 1 (Classes 1–5), Paper 2 (Classes 6–8)

Eligibility Criteria for Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test 2026 (Working Teachers)

Eligibility is limited to working teachers appointed on or before 01.09.2025 as Secondary Grade Teachers (SGT), BT Assistants, or equivalent cadres on time scale, consolidated, or part-time pay in specified departments and schools.

Educational Qualification for Paper 1 (Classes 1–5)

Candidates must possess the qualifications as per G.O.(Ms).No.13, School Education [SE3(1)] Department, dated 30.01.2020, including 10+2/HSC plus Diploma in Teacher Education/Diploma in Elementary Education or equivalent. This applies to Secondary Grade Teachers, BRTEs, and Special Education Teachers (IEDSS). In-service teachers in aided or unaided schools are also eligible if they meet NCTE norms.

Educational Qualification for Paper 2 (Classes 6–8)

Graduation in the relevant subject plus B.Ed. or equivalent, as per special rules for Tamil Nadu School Educational Subordinate Services. For Special Education Teachers, qualifications from G.O.(Ms).No.144, dated 17.06.2025 apply. Subject-specific requirements include relevant graduation for Mathematics/Science or Social Science teachers.

Age Limit and In-Service Relaxations

There is no upper age limit specified for TET eligibility. Relaxations in qualifying marks apply: 50% for BC/BCM/MBC/DNC/PWD and 40% for SC/SCA/ST.

Who Can Apply as a Working Teacher?

In-service teachers in government, government-aided, and recognized unaided private schools teaching Classes 1 to 8, including those under various departments like School Education, MBC, ADW, Tribal Welfare, and corporations. Qualified serving teachers opting for promotion must also apply.

TN TET 2026 Exam Pattern for Working Teachers

The exam pattern is identical for working and non-working candidates: 150 MCQs, 3 hours duration, no negative marking.

Tamil Nadu TET 2026 Exam Pattern – Paper 1

Paper 1 is for primary level (Classes 1–5).

Section Questions Marks Medium
Child Development and Pedagogy (6–11 yrs) 30 30 Tamil/English

Mathematics 30 30 Tamil/English
Environmental Studies 30 30 Tamil/English
Total 150 150 –

Tamil Nadu TET 2026 Exam Pattern – Paper 2

Paper 2 is for upper primary level (Classes 6–8).

Section Questions Marks Medium
Child Development and Pedagogy (11–14 yrs) 30 30 Tamil/English

Minimum Qualifying Marks for Working Teachers

General category: 60% (90/150). BC/BCM/MBC/DNC and PWD: 50% (75/150). SC/SCA/ST: 40% (60/150).

Tamil Nadu TET 2026 Syllabus for Working Teachers

The syllabus is based on the state-prescribed topics for Classes 1–8, with difficulty up to secondary/higher secondary stage.

TNTET 2026 Paper 1 Syllabus (Classes 1–5)

  • Child Development and Pedagogy: Stages of child development, learning theories, inclusive education, teaching–learning process, assessment and evaluation.
  • Language I (regional language): Reading comprehension, grammar, language skills, pedagogy of language development.
  • Language II – English: Comprehension, vocabulary, grammar, communication, English language pedagogy.
  • Mathematics: Number system, operations, fractions, decimals, geometry, measurement, data handling, pedagogy of mathematics.
  • Environmental Studies: Family and friends, food, water, travel, shelter, environment, resources, EVS pedagogy.

TNTET 2026 Paper 2 Syllabus (Classes 6–8)

  • Child Development and Pedagogy (11–14): Adolescent development, learning and motivation, classroom management, evaluation.
  • Language I and II: Similar components as Paper 1 but at higher difficulty level.
  • Subject-specific: Mathematics & Science – algebra, geometry, mensuration, statistics, basics of physics, chemistry, biology, pedagogy. Social Science – history, geography, civics, economics, social science pedagogy.

Note that the official TRB syllabus PDF must be followed strictly.

Application Process for Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test 2026 (Working Teachers)

Applications are online only via http://www.trb.tn.gov.in. Separate applications for Paper 1 and Paper 2 with fees.

  • Register with valid email and mobile number.
  • Fill details, upload photo (40-60 KB, JPG/JPEG/PNG), signature (20-40 KB), and certificates (250-300 KB PDF).
  • Pay fee: Rs.600/- (general) or Rs.300/- (SC/SCA/ST/PWD) via net banking/credit/debit card.
  • Use edit window if needed; submit by 10-04-2026.

Documents required:

  • 10th/SSLC, 12th/HSC, Diploma/B.Ed./UG certificates and mark sheets.
  • Community certificate, Differently Abled certificate.
  • Service Certificate (Annexure-I).

Exam Centres, Hall Ticket and Exam Day Guidelines

Exams in all districts; centre details in hall ticket. Download hall ticket from TRB website. Report early with ID proof; no electronic gadgets allowed. OMR-based; follow invigilator instructions.

TN TET 2026 Result, Certificate Validity and Use for Promotions

Results published on http://www.trb.tn.gov.in as qualified lists. Qualifying candidates receive TNTET certificates. Validity is lifetime as per norms. For working teachers, TET clearance is mandatory for promotions in Tamil Nadu government schools; it's an eligibility criterion for career progression.

Benefits of Clearing Tamil Nadu TET 2026 for Working Teachers

  • Eligibility for regularization and promotions in government and aided schools.
  • Compliance with Supreme Court directions making TET mandatory for Classes 1–8 teachers.
  • Better job security and mobility, eligibility for future recruitment drives.
  • Professional recognition and alignment with national teacher quality standards.

Preparation Strategy for Working Teachers – How to Crack TN TET 2026

Balance school duties with study by focusing on pedagogy sections. Use NCERT/Tamil Nadu textbooks for content revision.

  • Create a weekly timetable around school hours.
  • Revise core concepts from textbook levels you teach daily.
  • Use weekends for full-length mock tests.
  • Focus on weak sections identified from previous attempts.

Vacancy Details

Tamil Nadu Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (TANUVAS) is recruiting one Young Professional-I under an ICAR-NASF (Indian Council of Agricultural Research - National Agricultural Science Fund) funded project titled "Development and validation of recombinant multivalent porcine viral vaccine and DIVA diagnostics". This is a temporary contractual position based at the Vaccine Research Centre - Viral Vaccines, Centre for Animal Health Studies.

Position Vacancies Project Duration
Young Professional-I (YP-I) 1 ICAR-NASF Porcine Viral Vaccine Development 1 Year (Extendable up to 3 Years)

Eligibility Criteria

Educational Qualification

  • Essential: Graduation degree in any of the following disciplines from a recognized University:
    • Veterinary Sciences
    • Biotechnology
    • Microbiology
    • Applied Microbiology
    • Virology
    • Molecular Biology
    • Or related disciplines
  • Desirable: Post Graduate degree (Master's) in any of the above disciplines from a recognized University
  • All qualifications must be from recognized Universities only

Desirable Knowledge & Skills

  • Knowledge of animal cell culture techniques
  • Basic virology techniques
  • Molecular biology techniques
  • Bioinformatics knowledge

Age Limit

  • Minimum Age: 21 years
  • Maximum Age: 45 years
  • Age relaxation as per Government rules applicable

Important Dates

Event Date & Time
Notification Released 10.02.2026 (Tentative)
Walk-in Interview 20.02.2026 at 11:00 AM
Venue Vaccine Research Centre - Viral Vaccines, TANUVAS, Chennai
Registration/Entry Before 10:30 AM on interview day
Contract Duration 1 Year (extendable up to 3 years maximum)

  • Screening: All candidates appearing for walk-in-interview shall be screened and shortlisted before the interview
  • Written Test: A written test may be conducted before the interview to assess technical knowledge
  • Interview: Personal interview will be conducted to assess candidate's suitability, research interest, and technical competency
  • Document Verification: Original certificates will be verified during interview
  • Final Decision: The decision of the Director, Centre for Animal Health Studies, TANUVAS will be final and binding

Salary/Remuneration

  • Monthly Consolidated Pay: ₹30,000/- per month only
  • House Rent Allowance (HRA): NOT applicable
  • Nature of Payment: Consolidated fixed amount
  • No Additional Benefits: This is a contractual position under ICAR guidelines with no regular employment benefits

  • No Permanent Status: Selected candidates shall not have any right to claim for regular/permanent appointment under TANUVAS
  • Initial Duration: One year initial engagement
  • Extension: Extendable for two (02) more years (one year at a time) based on:
    • Organizational requirement
    • Performance evaluation of the candidate
    • Project continuation
    • Maximum limit: 3 years total (initial 1 year + 2 years extension)
  • Termination: TANUVAS holds no responsibility for payment of salary or appointment after expiry/termination of the project/scheme
  • Project Dependency: Engagement is purely dependent on ICAR-NASF project funding and continuity
  • ICAR Guidelines: General and other terms & conditions of ICAR guidelines for hiring technical manpower (Young Professional-I & II) shall apply (O.M. F. No. Agri.Edn.I-06/2020 dated 04/12/2020)

  • Date & Time: 20.02.2026 at 11:00 AM
  • Entry closes at: 10:30 AM (No entry after this time)
  • Venue: Vaccine Research Centre - Viral Vaccines, Centre for Animal Health Studies, TANUVAS, Madhavaram Milk Colony, Chennai – 600 051
  • Contact: Email: [email protected], Mobile: 9159168524

Documents Required

Important Instructions

  1. Original Certificates (MANDATORY):
    • Original Degree/Provisional Degree (PDC) certificate
    • Mark sheets of all semesters
    • Experience certificate(s) if applicable
  2. Self-Attested Copies: One complete set of self-attested copies of all:
    • Degree/PDC certificates
    • Mark sheets
    • Qualifications
    • Experience certificates
  3. Application: Bio Data/Application in prescribed format (provided in PDF)
  4. Photograph: Recent passport-size photograph
  5. Photo Identity: Photo ID issued by State/Central Government or Head of Institution (MANDATORY)
  6. NOC (if employed): No Objection Certificate from current employer (if candidate is under employment)
    • Candidates must be present AT LEAST 30 minutes before the scheduled interview time (by 10:30 AM)
    • No entry/registration will be permitted after 10:30 AM
    • Bring both original documents AND typed application in prescribed format
    • Candidates possessing only xerox/photocopy of degree certificates (without originals) shall NOT be allowed to attend the interview
    • Only those interested to serve at least for one year should attend the interview
    • Candidates under current employment must submit NOC during interview
    • All candidates will be screened and shortlisted before interview
    • A written test may be conducted before the interview
    • NO TA/DA will be paid to any candidate for attending the interview
    • Canvassing in any form will disqualify candidates

Vacancy Details

High Court of Allahabad has announced the recruitment of Special Judicial Magistrates for two districts in Uttar Pradesh. These positions are on a fixed honorarium basis with conveyance allowance. The recruitment is open for Government servants or former Government employees who possess legal qualifications or have extensive experience in legal affairs.

District Vacancy Position
Gonda 1 Special Judicial Magistrate
Jalaun (Orai) 1 Special Judicial Magistrate

Eligibility Criteria

Essential Qualifications

  • Status: Must be a Government servant (current or former) OR has held any post under the Government of India/State Government/Union Territory
  • Educational Qualification: Must possess:
    • Law degree (LL.B. from a recognized university), OR
    • Be well-experienced in relation to legal affairs to the satisfaction of the High Court
  • Professional Background: Experience in legal matters, judicial work, or administrative/legal roles under Government is an advantage

Term & Age

  • Term of Office: 4 years from the date of assumption of charge OR attaining the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier
  • Age Limit: No specific upper age limit mentioned, but term ends at age 70
  • Transferability: A candidate appointed for a specific district shall NOT be transferred to any other district under any circumstances

Previous SJM/SMM Experience

  • Ex-SJMs appointed by Government of Uttar Pradesh do NOT need to submit character roll entries
  • Ex-SJMs applying for re-appointment must enclose four best judgments delivered while holding the post of SJM/SMM

Important Dates

Event Date
Notification Released 09.02.2026
Application Submission Last Date 13-04-2026
Selection Process Merit-based by High Court
Term of Office 4 Years or Age 70 years

Selection Process

  • Application Scrutiny: All applications are submitted to the respective District Judge who conducts preliminary scrutiny
  • District Judge Review: The District Judge reviews applications and forwards only those he finds fit for the SJM post to the High Court with his remarks
  • High Court Evaluation: The High Court evaluates forwarded applications based on qualifications, experience, and legal expertise
  • Merit-Based Selection: Selection is based on merit, qualifications, Government service record, and experience in legal matters
  • Final Appointment: Appointment is made by the High Court through formal order of the Court

Salary/Remuneration

  • Fixed Honorarium: ₹45,000/- per month (fixed, subject to correction and updation by High Court)
  • Conveyance Allowance: ₹5,000/- per month for official travel and conveyance
  • Total Monthly Remuneration: ₹50,000/- per month (base honorarium + conveyance)
  • Payment: Subject to correction and updation from time to time as per High Court guidelines

How to Apply

Application Preparation

  1. Download the Application Form from the official High Court notification PDF
  2. Fill all columns of the application form in block letters (all columns are compulsory)
  3. Affix a self-attested recent passport-size photograph
  4. Provide complete and accurate information including:
    • Full name, father's name, date of birth
    • Current and permanent residential addresses with PIN codes
    • Email address and mobile number
    • Details of posts held under the Government (designation, pay scale, duration, retirement date)
    • Educational qualifications (High School, Intermediate, Graduation, LL.B., and any other qualifications)
    • Whether previously worked as SJM/SMM with year-wise details and annual confidential report percentages
  5. Mention whether any criminal case is pending or FIR lodged
  6. Sign the declaration that all information provided is correct

Required Documents (Self-Attested)

  • Photocopies of all relevant documents mentioned in the application
  • Character roll entries of the last 5 years of Government service (if applicable)
  • Law degree certificate and other educational qualification certificates
  • Copy of Gazette notification of Government service record
  • For ex-SJMs applying for re-appointment: Four best judgments delivered as SJM/SMM
  • Annual Confidential Reports (ACR) for the last 5 years (if available)
  • Self-attested photograph (4x6 cm)

Submission Mode

  1. Applicants must submit their applications OFFLINE directly to the respective District Judge of the district for which they are applying
  2. Do NOT send applications directly to the High Court — applications sent directly to High Court will be rejected
  3. Submit to the following District Judges based on your choice:
    • For Gonda: District Judge, Gonda District Court
    • For Jalaun: District Judge, Jalaun District Court
  4. Ensure all documents are complete and properly organized
  5. Keep a copy of submitted application for reference

Selection Process

  • Recruitment of teaching staff will be compiled at district level post-wise / subject-wise / category-wise; applications will be invited accordingly.

  • Merit weightage (Quality Marks) will be calculated as follows:
    • High School: Percentage of marks obtained × 10/100
    • Intermediate: Percentage of marks obtained × 10/100
    • Graduation: Percentage of marks obtained × 20/100
    • Post-Graduation: Percentage of marks obtained × 20/100
    • Training (B.Ed/M.Ed etc.): Percentage of marks in theory & practical × 30/100
  • If two or more candidates have equal merit points, the older candidate (higher age) will be placed higher in the merit list.
  • If merit and age are both equal, the candidate whose name appears earlier in English alphabetical order will be ranked higher.
  • Selection for Head Cook, Assistant Cook, Peon and Watchman will be based on interview.
  • Original documents/certificates of selected staff will be verified from the concerned Board/Institution at the time of appointment.
  • Original academic records will be preserved/safeguarded at the District Project Office. Salary will be paid only after document verification.

  • Incomplete, unsigned, or applications without required attachments will be rejected.

  • Reservation benefits will be as per State Government norms. OBC / SC / ST / EWS certificates issued by a competent authority must be attached; otherwise reservation benefits will not be given.
  • Candidates with moral turpitude, character/criminal convictions, or declared bankrupt are not eligible.

How to Apply

Strong PostgreSQL and PostGIS skills covering query optimization, indexing, and partitioning are required. Experience with Redis, gRPC, and Protocol Buffers is desirable. Proficiency in LLM integration, AI agent orchestration, RAG architectures, and vector databases is highly valued. Embedded systems development is a plus. Candidates must be capable of package-level engineering — authoring libraries, SDKs, and CLI tools. Proficiency with Uber's H3 spatial indexing and geospatial pipelines is expected.
